law_name: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
applies_to: All companies processing EU residents' data
key_requirements: Lawful basis, consent, data subject rights
enforcement_authority: European Data Protection Board & National DPAs
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: GDPR does not apply to deceased persons' data; Member States may set rules (recital 27)
research_exemption: Archiving, scientific/historical research and statistics: safeguards incl. minimisation/pseudonymisation; Union/national derogations from rights (art. 89; also arts. 5(1)(b), 14(5)(b), 17(3)(d))
genetic_data: Special category: processing prohibited unless an art. 9(2) basis applies (e.g. explicit consent, 9(2)(a)); Member States may add conditions (art. 9(4))
notes: Extraterritorial applicability
pending_change: Digital Omnibus: GDPR amendments proposed by the Commission on 19 Nov 2025; not adopted

law_name: California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (CCPA/CPRA)
key_requirements: Disclosure, opt-out rights
enforcement_authority: California Privacy Protection Agency (CalPrivacy) and California Attorney General
penalties_range: USD 2,663 per violation; USD 7,988 per intentional violation or involving minors under 16 (inflation-adjusted) (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Deletion right exception for public-interest peer-reviewed research where deletion would impair it (s. 1798.105(d)(6)); 'research' defined in s. 1798.140, no commercial purpose
genetic_data: Genetic data is 'sensitive personal information' (s. 1798.140(ae)); consumers may limit its use to necessary purposes
notes: CPRA amendments effective 2023-01-01; ADMT and opt-out-signal rules due 2027-01-01

law_name: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)
key_requirements: Parental consent required
enforcement_authority: FTC & State AGs
penalties_range: Up to $43,280 per violation
research_exemption: No research exception found among the exceptions to verifiable parental consent (16 CFR 312.5(c)) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: 2025 amendments add biometric identifiers incl. genetic data (e.g. DNA sequences) to 'personal information' (16 CFR 312.2); compliance by 22 Apr 2026
notes: FTC Rule amended 2025: biometrics in PI, retention/security programs; full compliance 2026-04-22

law_name: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA)
key_requirements: Lawful collection, accuracy
enforcement_authority: Privacy Commissioner of Canada
penalties_range: Up to $100,000 CAD
deceased_data: Disclosure without consent allowed after the earlier of 100 years after record creation or 20 years after death (s. 7(3)(h))
research_exemption: Use without consent for statistical or scholarly study/research if consent impracticable and Commissioner notified (s. 7(2)(c), disclosure s. 7(3)(f)); disclosure to archival institutions (s. 7(3)(g))
genetic_data: No statutory rule; OPC guidance treats genetic and biometric data as generally sensitive, express consent expected
notes: Private sector national standard
pending_change: Bill C-36 (Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act), tabled 15 Jun 2026, would replace PIPEDA Part 1; not enacted

law_name: Data Protection Act 2018 (DPA 2018)
key_requirements: GDPR-aligned requirements
enforcement_authority: Information Commission (successor to the Information Commissioner's Office under DUAA 2025 Part 6)
penalties_range: Up to £20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: personal data means data on an identified or identifiable living individual (s. 3(2))
research_exemption: Exemptions from access, rectification, restriction, objection for research/statistics (Sch. 2 para 27) and archiving in public interest (para 28), where rights would prejudice purposes
genetic_data: Special category data (UK GDPR art. 9; defined art. 4(13)); needs art. 6 basis plus art. 9 condition, and DPA Sch. 1 condition where required
notes: Amended by Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; new ICO powers in force 2026-02-05 (SI 2026/82)

law_name: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (LGPD)
key_requirements: Lawful basis & consent
enforcement_authority: Agencia Nacional de Protecao de Dados (ANPD) - regulatory agency under Lei 15.352/2026
penalties_range: Up to 50M BRL or 2% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: ANPD Nota Tecnica 3/2023/CGF holds LGPD does not apply to deceased persons (Civil Code art. 6); protection via succession/personality rights
research_exemption: Studies by research body without consent, anonymised where possible (art. 7 IV; sensitive data art. 11 II c); public-health studies (art. 13); academic use partly excluded (art. 4 II b)
genetic_data: Sensitive personal data when linked to a natural person (art. 5 II); processing only on art. 11 bases
notes: Lei 15.352 of 2026-02-25 made ANPD an autonomous regulatory agency; also enforces ECA Digital

law_name: Act on Protection of Personal Information (APPI)
key_requirements: Lawful purpose notice
enforcement_authority: Personal Information Protection Commission
penalties_range: Up to ¥1M penalty
deceased_data: Not covered: personal information is information relating to a living individual (art. 2(1))
research_exemption: Since 2022 amendment (effective 1 Apr 2022) academic research institutions get per-obligation exceptions instead of a blanket exemption
genetic_data: Genomic data can be personal information (individual identification code, art. 2(2)); not confirmed as special care-required (art. 2(3)) (unconfirmed)
notes: 2026 amendment adds administrative fines; effective date by cabinet order (<=2 yrs)
pending_change: Amendment Act No. 56 of 2026 (administrative fines) promulgated 17 Jul 2026; not yet in force

law_name: Privacy Act 1988
jurisdiction: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
key_requirements: Australian Privacy Principles
enforcement_authority: Australian Information Commissioner
penalties_range: Up to AUD $50M
deceased_data: Not covered: the Privacy Act does not apply to personal information of a deceased individual
research_exemption: Medical/health research without consent under NHMRC guidelines approved under ss. 95 (agencies) and 95A (organisations)
genetic_data: Genetic information is 'sensitive information' (s. 6) with higher protection
notes: Amended by POLA Act 2024 (statutory privacy tort, ADM transparency); Tranche 2 bill in consultation
pending_change: Tranche 2 reform: Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026 exposure draft released 31 Aug 2026; not law

law_name: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023
key_requirements: Consent & lawful processing
enforcement_authority: Data Protection Board of India
penalties_range: Up to ₹250 Cr penalty
deceased_data: Data principal may nominate an individual to exercise rights on death or incapacity (s. 14)
research_exemption: Act does not apply to processing for research, archiving or statistics if per Second Schedule standards and no decision on a specific individual (s. 17(2)(b))
genetic_data: No specific rule: no sensitive or genetic data category; general consent regime applies
notes: DPDP Rules 2025 notified Nov 2025; DPB established; substantive duties apply ~May 2027
pending_change: DPDP Rules 2025 (Nov 2025) bring most obligations into force in phases over 18 months

law_name: Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA)
key_requirements: Conditions & consent
enforcement_authority: South Africa Information Regulator
penalties_range: Up to R10M or 10% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: personal information relates to an identifiable, living natural person or existing juristic person (s. 1)
research_exemption: Further processing allowed for historical, statistical or research purposes if not published in identifiable form (s. 15(3)(e)); special information subject to s. 27
genetic_data: Not named in s. 26; health and biometric information are special personal information (university guide lists DNA) (unconfirmed)
notes: Africa's comprehensive privacy law

law_name: Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP 2025)
key_requirements: Lawful processing & consent
enforcement_authority: Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno (took over from INAI, dissolved in 2025)
penalties_range: Up to 320,000 UMA (~MXN 36M at 2025 UMA); doubled for sensitive data
research_exemption: Consent not required for data subjected to prior dissociation, useful for statistics/research (art. 10) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Sensitive data includes genetic information; express written consent required
notes: Replaced the 2010 LFPDPPP; date shown is DOF publication (entry into force not confirmed). INAI was dissolved

law_name: Federal Data Protection Act (FADP)
key_requirements: Lawful basis & transparency
enforcement_authority: Swiss DPA Commissioner
penalties_range: Up to CHF 100k penalty
deceased_data: No FADP rule: the deceased-persons provision of the draft was dropped from the revised Act
research_exemption: Overriding interest for research, planning, statistics if results published non-identifiably (art. 31(2)(e)); research privilege for federal bodies (art. 39)
genetic_data: Sensitive personal data (art. 5 lit. c), added in revised FADP
notes: GDPR-aligned European standard

law_name: Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
key_requirements: Consent & purpose limitation
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC)
penalties_range: Up to 10% of annual Singapore turnover (if >SGD 10m) or SGD 1 million, whichever higher
deceased_data: Disclosure and protection provisions apply to individuals dead 10 years or fewer (s. 4(4))
research_exemption: Research exception to consent (Second Schedule Part 2): identifiable form necessary, consent impracticable, public-interest benefit
notes: Amended 2020 (in force 2021-02-01): mandatory breach notification, higher fines from 2022-10-01

law_name: Privacy Act 2020
key_requirements: IPP 3A: notify individuals when personal info collected indirectly (from 2026-05-01)
enforcement_authority: Privacy Commissioner NZ
penalties_range: Up to NZD 200k penalty
deceased_data: Not covered: individual means a living natural person (s. 7) (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Disclosure for statistical or research purposes if not published in identifiable form (IPP 11 exception)
genetic_data: Health Information Privacy Code 2020 governs health/genetic information; no specific rule confirmed in Act (unconfirmed)
notes: Amended by Privacy Amendment Act 2025; IPP 3A in force 2026-05-01

law_name: Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA)
key_requirements: Purpose limitation & consent
enforcement_authority: KISA & Supervisory Authorities
penalties_range: Up to 3% of total revenue; up to 10% for repeat intentional/grossly negligent violations, breaches affecting >=10m people, or ignoring PIPC orders
deceased_data: Not covered: personal information concerns living individuals (art. 2(1)); may protect bereaved family's data
research_exemption: Pseudonymised data may be processed without consent for statistics, scientific research, public-interest archiving (art. 28-2); most rights excluded (art. 28-7)
genetic_data: Sensitive information: DNA information from genetic testing (art. 23; Enforcement Decree art. 18); separate consent or legal basis required
notes: 2026 amendment in force 2026-09-11: 10% revenue fines; CEO named ultimately responsible

law_name: Personal Data Protection Law (Decree No. 144 of 2024)
key_requirements: Express informed consent (Arts. 5, 27); ARCO-POL rights; privacy officer; transfers only to adequate countries (Art. 44); 72h breach notice (firm summary)
retention_period: Art. 5(h) temporality principle: keep data only for the period needed to achieve processing purposes; consent must state storage period (Art. 5)
enforcement_authority: Agencia de Ciberseguridad del Estado (ACE), per Human Rights Watch; another source names the new National Digital Authority
penalties_range: Up to 40 monthly minimum wages, commerce sector (~USD 14,600) for very serious infractions (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Art. 2 excludes: purely family/domestic processing (non-commercial); public security, defence, State security, crime prevention/investigation; public registries
notes: First general data-protection law (approved 12 Nov 2024); date shown is gazette publication. The earlier row described a law that does not exist

law_name: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
key_requirements: GDPR + French amendments
enforcement_authority: CNIL (National Commission)
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: Post-mortem directives on retention/erasure/communication; heirs may act absent directives (arts. 84-85 Loi Informatique et Libertes); health research on deceased unless prior refusal (art. 86)
research_exemption: Archiving, scientific/historical research and statistics regime (arts. 78-79); rights limitations via decree 2019-536 art. 116
genetic_data: Sensitive data under art. 6 I Loi Informatique et Libertes; processing prohibited save exceptions
notes: National complement: Loi n 78-17 Informatique et Libertes (amended 2018); regulator CNIL

law_name: Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD)
key_requirements: GDPR implementation
enforcement_authority: AEPD (Spanish Authority)
penalties_range: Up to €10M or 3% revenue
deceased_data: Law excludes deceased, but relatives and heirs may request access, rectification, erasure unless prohibited by deceased (art. 3)
research_exemption: Health and genetic data research under DA 17 (incl. pseudonymised reuse); public statistics (art. 25); art. 89 GDPR safeguards
genetic_data: Health and genetic data processing covered by GDPR art. 9.2 g-j under laws listed in DA 17 (e.g. Ley 14/2007)
notes: GDPR implementation

law_name: Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG)
key_requirements: GDPR + German provisions
enforcement_authority: German Data Protection Authorities
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
research_exemption: Special categories allowed for research/statistics without consent; rights under arts. 15,16,18,21 restricted (s. 27 BDSG); archiving (s. 28)
genetic_data: Special category (GDPR art. 9); national opening clause with safeguards (s. 22 BDSG)
notes: GDPR implementation
pending_change: BDSG reform bill (BT-Drs. 21/7732, Aug 2026) pending; not enacted

law_name: Personal Data Protection Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003, Codice privacy)
key_requirements: GDPR + Italian law
enforcement_authority: Garante (Italian Authority)
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: GDPR rights (arts. 15-22) exercisable by persons with own interest, agent or family reasons unless deceased forbade in writing (art. 2-terdecies)
research_exemption: Medical/biomedical/epidemiological research without consent with ethics committee opinion and Garante safeguards (art. 110, amended 2024; Garante provv. 298/2024)
genetic_data: Processing only with Garante safeguard measures, renewed at least every two years (art. 2-septies; provv. 146/2019 annex 4)
notes: D.lgs. 196/2003 as amended by D.lgs. 101/2018 (GDPR adaptation, in force 2018-09-19)

law_name: GDPR Implementation Act (Uitvoeringswet AVG, UAVG)
key_requirements: GDPR applies: lawful basis, data subject rights, breach notification
enforcement_authority: Dutch Authority for Data Protection
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens states AVG does not apply directly to deceased persons' data (recital 27)
research_exemption: Special categories for public-interest research/statistics if consent impossible (art. 24 UAVG); rights 15,16,18 may be set aside (art. 44)
genetic_data: Prohibited in principle; allowed under same conditions as art. 24 or explicit legal basis (art. 28 UAVG)
notes: UAVG amended by Verzamelwet gegevensbescherming 2026; AP must publish fines; in force TBD

law_name: Law of 30 July 2018 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data
key_requirements: GDPR applies: lawful basis, data subject rights, breach notification
enforcement_authority: Belgian Data Protection Authority (APD/GBA)
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: No specific Belgian rules on deceased persons' data; GDPR covers living persons only
research_exemption: Title 4 regime for archiving, scientific/historical research and statistics: derogations from data subject rights with safeguards (pseudonymisation, DPO art. 190, records arts. 191-192, info art. 193)
genetic_data: Special category (art. 9 GDPR); controller must keep list of categories of persons with access to genetic/biometric/health data and their roles, given to DPA on request
notes: GDPR implementation

law_name: Act (2018:218) with supplementary provisions to the GDPR (Dataskyddslagen)
key_requirements: GDPR + Swedish law
enforcement_authority: Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY)
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: GDPR recital 27 excludes deceased persons; no specific rule found in Act 2018:218 (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Sensitive data may be processed for research only after approval by the Ethical Review Authority (Ethical Review Act 2003:460, s. 6); Act 2018:218 adds archive/research exceptions to rights (chs. 3-4)
genetic_data: Special category (art. 9 GDPR); Genetic Integrity Act (2006:351) s. 4 complements GDPR, with Act 2018:218 applying unless it provides otherwise
notes: GDPR implementation

law_name: Act of 10 May 2018 on the Protection of Personal Data
key_requirements: GDPR applies: lawful basis, data subject rights, breach notification
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Office (UODO)
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: Poland added no rules for deceased persons, so GDPR (living persons only) applies by default
research_exemption: Not in the 2018 Act: Higher Education and Science Act art. 469b(2) allows special-category data for research if results are non-identifying; anonymise once purpose reached
genetic_data: Special category under art. 9 GDPR; no specific rule found in the 2018 Act (unconfirmed)
notes: GDPR implementation

law_name: Act No. 110/2019 Coll. on the Processing of Personal Data
key_requirements: GDPR compliance + amendments
enforcement_authority: Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ)
penalties_range: Up to €20M or 4% revenue
deceased_data: No Czech-specific rule found; GDPR (recitals 27, 160) does not apply to deceased persons (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Section 16 sets conditions for processing (incl. art. 9(1) special categories) for scientific/historical research and statistics, with safeguards
genetic_data: Special category (art. 9(1) GDPR); may be processed for research under Section 16 conditions; no other specific rule found (unconfirmed)
notes: GDPR implementation

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (PDPL)
scope: Processing of personal data in Vietnam and of Vietnamese data subjects, incl. foreign entities
applies_to: Domestic and foreign organisations, agencies and individuals processing personal data
key_requirements: Consent (explicit for sensitive data); processing and transfer impact assessments (DPIA/TIA); designate DPO/department; cross-border transfer rules
data_categories: Basic and sensitive personal data (e.g. health, biometric, genetic, location)
retention_period: Art. 3 principles: data stored only for period consistent with processing purpose unless law provides otherwise; delete/de-identify when purpose ends
enforcement_authority: Department of Cybersecurity and High-Tech Crime Prevention (A05) - Ministry of Public Security
penalties_range: Up to 5% of prior-year revenue (cross-border violations); up to 10x illegal gain (data trading); up to VND 3 billion other
exemptions: Micro-enterprises/household businesses exempt from DPO and DPIA; 5-year grace for small firms/startups (not if sensitive data, data services or >=100k subjects)
notes: Law 91/2025/QH15 replaces Decree 13/2023; guided by Decree 356/2025; sanctions decree 330/2026 from 2026-08-19

law_name: Federal Law No. 152-FZ on Personal Data

penalties_range: Up to RUB 15M per leak (>100k subjects or special categories); repeat leaks: 1-3% of revenue, min RUB 20M, max RUB 500M

law_name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)
key_requirements: Expanded grounds for special-category data; tiered cross-border transfers (adequacy / SCCs notified to Board in 5 days / BCRs); VERBIS registration
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK)
penalties_range: Up to TRY 1M fine
deceased_data: Not covered: 'data subject' is a living natural person; Board decision 2019/273 rejected a spouse's art. 11 request for a deceased's records
research_exemption: Law does not apply to data anonymized for official statistics or for research, planning and statistics (art. 28(1)(c))
genetic_data: Special category (art. 6): processing prohibited unless explicit consent or another art. 6(3) exception (as amended 2024)
notes: Amended by Law 7499 (in force 2024-06-01): new transfer regime, SCC notification, special categories

law_name: Personal Data Protection Law
key_requirements: Consent & transparency
enforcement_authority: Saudi PDPL Authority
penalties_range: Up to SAR 5M (doubled for repeat); sensitive-data disclosure: up to SAR 3M and 2 years prison
deceased_data: Covered: definition of personal data includes a deceased person's data if it can identify them or a family member (art. 1)
research_exemption: Collection/processing for scientific, research or statistical purposes without consent if data is non-identifying, identifiers destroyed, or required by law (art. 27; Impl. Regs art. 30)
genetic_data: Sensitive data (genetic information listed): explicit consent or specific legal exception required; legitimate interest not available

law_name: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data
key_requirements: Lawful processing
enforcement_authority: UAE Data Office
penalties_range: Fines up to AED 500k
deceased_data: Unclear: law defines personal data by reference to a natural person and does not say whether data of deceased persons remain covered
research_exemption: Consent not required for processing for archival purposes or scientific, historical and statistical studies under applicable UAE law (art. 4)
genetic_data: Sensitive personal data includes genetic data/condition (art. 1); enhanced protection, consent or art. 4 exception required
notes: UAE privacy law

law_name: Privacy Protection Law
key_requirements: Lawful collection & transparency
enforcement_authority: Privacy Protection Authority (PPA)
penalties_range: Administrative fines up to NIS 320,000 per violation (higher if aggravated / per-data-subject based); criminal penalties
deceased_data: No express rule; commentators say the dead have no privacy rights under the Law; courts recognized a separate publicity right surviving death 25+ years (Dali, 2016) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Governed by separate Genetic Information Law 5761-2000: testing needs informed consent/authorization; genetic data also sensitive under the Privacy Law
notes: Amendment 13 effective 2025-08-14: PPA fining powers, DPO duty, broader definitions

law_name: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA)
scope: Processing of personal data in Nigeria or of data subjects in Nigeria, incl. foreign controllers
applies_to: Data controllers and processors; those of major importance must register with NDPC and appoint a DPO
key_requirements: Section 24 processing principles; lawful basis/consent; breach notice to NDPC within 72 hours; registration of major-importance controllers
data_categories: Personal data and sensitive personal data (extendable by NDPC directive)
retention_period: Storage limitation principle (s.24); no fixed period found
enforcement_authority: Nigeria Data Protection Commission
penalties_range: Up to the higher of NGN 10M or 2% of annual gross revenue (major importance); NGN 2M or 2% for others
exemptions: Criminal investigation/prosecution, national public health emergencies, national security by competent authorities
notes: Replaces NDPR 2019; commenced on signing; GAID 2025 directive effective 2025-09-19

law_name: Data Protection Act (DSG)

enforcement_authority: Data Protection Authority (Datenschutzstelle)

deceased_data: No specific national rules on deceased persons' data (GDPR recital 27: living persons only); professional secrecy still applies

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (Law No. 2297-VI)

notes: GDPR-style bill 8153 passed 1st reading only (Nov 2024); 2010 law still applies

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (PDP Law)

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (Law No. 124/2024)

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (LPDP)

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (Law No. 195/2024)

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (Law No. 3144/2023)
