law_name: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 (PDPP)
applies_to: Public & private data controllers and processors
key_requirements: Authority authorisation before processing, breach notification within 72 hours, cross-border transfer limits
retention_period: Art. 15 storage limitation (unofficial text): retain for reasonable period needed for purpose or as set by law; longer for law, consent, research/statistics
enforcement_authority: Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA)
penalties_range: Up to 4% of worldwide turnover (entities); up to 10 years' imprisonment and ETB 300000 fines
notes: Parliament passed it 4 Apr 2024; date shown is gazette publication; ECA directives pending

law_name: Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (CQLR c. P-39.1), as amended by Law 25 (S.Q. 2021, c. 25)
jurisdiction: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI)
scope: Individuals in Quebec whose personal information is held by enterprises operating in Quebec
applies_to: Private-sector enterprises carrying on an enterprise in Quebec (the Act's s.1), including those outside Quebec handling Quebec residents' data
key_requirements: Consent that is clear, free and specific (s.14); rights of access, rectification, portability and de-indexation; privacy impact assessments for projects and cross-border transfers (s.3.3, 17); mandatory reporting of confidentiality incidents to CAI and individuals (s.3.5); designated person in charge of personal information (s.3.1)
data_categories: Personal information; sensitive information (medical; biometric or otherwise intimate; s.12)
retention_period: Keep only as long as necessary for the purposes; then destroy or anonymize (s.23)
enforcement_authority: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI)
penalties_range: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 10M or 2% of worldwide turnover; penal fines up to CAD 25M or 4% of worldwide turnover; private right of action with punitive damages of at least CAD 1,000 for intentional or grave fault
exemptions: Journalistic, historical or genealogical material for the legitimate information of the public (s.1); public bodies covered by the public-sector Act; business contact information (s.1)
deceased_data: Not generally covered (living individuals); an enterprise may communicate information to a deceased person's spouse or close relatives where it helps their grieving process (added by Law 25) (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Information may be released without consent for study or research purposes after a privacy impact assessment and written agreement (s.21-21.0.2)
genetic_data: No specific genetic rule; falls under sensitive information (medical or intimate) requiring express consent (s.12, 12 para 2) (unconfirmed)
notes: Law 25 assented 2021-09-22; phased entry into force: 2022-09-22 (privacy officer, incident reporting, biometrics disclosure), 2023-09-22 (main obligations: consent, privacy policy, PIAs, transparency, automated decisions, private right of action, penalties), 2024-09-22 (data portability). Sources differ on exact phase contents; original Act P-39.1 dates from 1993/1994.

law_name: Personal Information Protection Act (SA 2003, c. P-6.5)
jurisdiction: Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta (OIPC)
scope: Individuals in Alberta whose personal information is handled by private-sector organizations
applies_to: Private-sector organizations in Alberta: corporations, unincorporated associations, trade unions, partnerships, individuals acting in a commercial capacity (s.1)
key_requirements: Consent for collection, use and disclosure with reasonable purposes (s.7-8, 11-19); access and correction rights (s.24-25); mandatory notification of the Commissioner of incidents posing a real risk of significant harm (s.34.1)
retention_period: Retain only as long as reasonable for legal or business purposes (s.35)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta (OIPC)
penalties_range: Offence fines up to CAD 100,000 for organizations and CAD 10,000 for individuals (s.59); Commissioner has binding order-making power but no administrative penalties
exemptions: Personal or domestic use, journalistic/artistic/literary purposes, public bodies under FOIP, health information under the Health Information Act (s.4)
deceased_data: Not specifically covered; the Act protects identifiable individuals (living); no express deceased rule (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Disclosure without consent allowed for research with conditions (s.22), and for archival purposes (s.21) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: No specific rule (unconfirmed)
notes: Legislative committee review of PIPA completed 2025 recommending alignment with global standards and administrative penalties; no replacement private-sector act confirmed as of 2026-10. Bills 33/34 (Dec 2024) replace only the public-sector FOIP Act.

law_name: Personal Information Protection Act (SBC 2003, c. 63)
jurisdiction: Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for British Columbia (OIPC BC)
scope: Individuals in British Columbia whose personal information is held by private organizations
applies_to: Private organizations (corporations, partnerships, unincorporated associations, trade unions, trusts, not-for-profits) collecting, using or disclosing personal information in BC; federal PIPEDA prevails for federal works
key_requirements: Consent and reasonable purposes (s.6-8, 10-12, 14-18); access and correction rights (s.23-24); reasonable security safeguards (s.34); no mandatory breach notification in the current Act
retention_period: Retain for at least one year after use for decisions about the individual; destroy or anonymize when no longer needed for legal or business purposes (s.35)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for British Columbia (OIPC BC)
penalties_range: Offence fines up to CAD 100,000 for organizations and CAD 10,000 for individuals (s.56); Commissioner can investigate, audit and issue binding orders but has no administrative monetary penalty power
exemptions: Personal or domestic purposes, journalistic/artistic/literary purposes, public bodies under FOIPPA, business contact information (s.3)
deceased_data: Information about a person dead 20 years or more is excluded from the Act (s.3(2)), so deceased persons are covered for about 20 years (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Disclosure without consent allowed for research or statistical purposes under conditions (s.21) and archival or historical purposes (s.20) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: No specific rule (unconfirmed)
notes: OIPC and a 2020-21 special committee urged reform (mandatory breach notification, administrative penalties); no replacement act confirmed. Enactment date sources conflict (Royal Assent reported both May and October 2003).

law_name: Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), as amended and supplemented in 2019 to implement GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
scope: Data subjects (natural persons) in Bulgaria / processed by Bulgarian controllers
applies_to: All public and private controllers and processors; must be read together with GDPR
key_requirements: GDPR legal bases and data-subject rights; digital consent age 14; national rules on DPO, certification and CPDP supervision; breach notification under GDPR art. 33
data_categories: Personal data; special categories of data; criminal-conviction data
retention_period: No longer than necessary for the purposes (GDPR art. 5(1)(e)); PDPA adds national retention rules for some data
enforcement_authority: Commission for Personal Data Protection (CPDP)
penalties_range: Up to EUR 20M or 4% of turnover under GDPR art. 83; residual PDPA violations up to BGN 5,000 (doubled on repetition); largest fine to date about EUR 2.55M (National Revenue Agency 2019)
exemptions: Journalism, academic and artistic expression, and archiving in the public interest (national rules under GDPR art. 85); household use; security and criminal-justice processing under separate regime (unconfirmed)
deceased_data: Not covered by main rules, but art. 25f PDPA allows processing of deceased persons' data only on a legal basis with safeguards
research_exemption: Further use for scientific or historical research and statistics allowed if permitted by EU or Bulgarian law, necessary and proportionate, with safeguards (GDPR art. 89)
genetic_data: Special category under GDPR art. 9; explicit consent or another art. 9(2) ground required
notes: GDPR applies directly (EU member); PDPA is the national implementing act. Amended again since 2019 (e.g. 2023); consolidated text not checked.

law_name: Organic Law No. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 on the Protection of Personal Data
scope: Natural persons whose personal data is processed in Tunisia
applies_to: All public and private controllers and processors
key_requirements: Express written consent subject to exceptions (art. 27 on capacity); prior declaration or INPDP authorization for sensitive data and cross-border transfers; data-subject rights of access, rectification and objection
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (racial and genetic origin, religious beliefs, political/philosophical/trade-union affiliation, health) (arts. 5 and 14)
enforcement_authority: National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (INPDP)
penalties_range: Criminal sanctions; e.g. failure to meet prior notification duties: 1 year imprisonment and TND 5,000 fine; some offences up to 2 years (sources vary) (unconfirmed)
exemptions: UNKNOWN (public security and defence processing has special rules; art. 14 exceptions not verified) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic origin is sensitive data; processing generally prohibited unless an exception or INPDP authorization applies (arts. 14 and 5)
notes: Replacement bill (Proposal Organic Law No. 095/2025, deposited July 2025) was still before committees at last check; not law. Frameworks value from background knowledge, not from a result seen.

law_name: Law No. 18-07 of 10 June 2018 on the Protection of Natural Persons in the Processing of Personal Data, as amended by Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025
scope: Natural persons whose data is processed in Algeria
applies_to: Public and private operators in Algeria, including foreign operators using automated means located in Algeria
key_requirements: Explicit consent before collection; ANPDP declaration or authorization for certain processing; transfers abroad need ANPDP authorization and adequate protection (art. 44-45)
enforcement_authority: National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (ANPDP)
penalties_range: Criminal: up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to DZD 500,000 (some sources DZD 20,000-1,000,000)
exemptions: Art. 45 derogations from transfer rules; state security and criminal-justice processing (not verified in detail) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Likely sensitive data under art. 9 (not verified) (unconfirmed)
notes: Law 25-11 of 2025 reportedly adds DPO and DPIA duties; only one vendor page says so, unconfirmed. Main obligations enforceable from 2023 when ANPDP was set up.

law_name: Law No. 81 of 2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data
scope: Individuals whose personal data is processed (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Consent or other legal basis, purpose limitation, security; licence or authorization from the Ministry of Economy and Trade for processing certain data categories (unconfirmed)
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data requiring licence (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Ministry of Economy and Trade (no dedicated authority; some sources name Ministry of Telecommunications / TRA)
penalties_range: Not specified
notes: Mixed e-commerce/e-signature law with a personal data chapter; no independent DPA; sources conflict on regulator.

law_name: Personal Data Protection Ordinance, 2025 (Ordinance No. 61 of 2025)
scope: Data subjects (individuals) whose personal data is processed
applies_to: Controllers and processors of personal data (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Explicit consent before collection, storage, transfer or use of personal data; data-subject ownership/rights; administrative fines, compensation and criminal penalties for violations
enforcement_authority: National Data Governance Authority
penalties_range: Administrative fines, compensation and criminal penalties; amounts not confirmed (unconfirmed)
notes: Issued as an ordinance by the interim government; some sections reportedly take effect 18 months after gazette notification (Daily Star); parliamentary ratification unconfirmed; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 on Personal Data and Their Protection
jurisdiction: Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Aerospace Industry
applies_to: Owners and operators of personal databases, and third parties processing personal data
key_requirements: Consent of the data subject for collection and processing; breach notification to the authority since 1 July 2024 (Law No. 44-VIII of 11 Dec 2023); 2026 amendments add automated-decision limits and breach register
data_categories: Personal data (general and restricted-access); biometric data
enforcement_authority: Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Aerospace Industry (MDDIAI)
penalties_range: Administrative fines under the Code of Administrative Offences in MCI units (reported 100-10,000 MCI); criminal liability including imprisonment up to 5 years (unconfirmed)
notes: Amended 2024 and 2026 (definition of personal data from 11 July 2026; breach register from 25 Aug 2026); penalty figures from secondary sources conflict

law_name: Law No. 58 of 14 April 2008 on Personal Information
jurisdiction: State Agency for Personal Data Protection
applies_to: Holders (owners) and processors of personal data arrays
key_requirements: Consent of the subject; mandatory registration of personal data arrays and holders with the State Agency; security of personal data
enforcement_authority: State Agency for Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Protection Agency)
penalties_range: Administrative fines reported from May 2025, unverified (unconfirmed)
deceased_data: On state registration of death the subject gets 'deceased' status and data must be archived and stored (2022 amendment, Law No. 61); law replaced by Digital Code No. 178 from 5 Feb 2026
genetic_data: No specific rule: law has no clear definition of sensitive personal data; genetic data not named (unconfirmed)
notes: Last amendments seen 29 Nov 2021; EUI database says authority not yet established, conflicting with other sources

law_name: Law No. 1537 of 3 August 2018 on Personal Data Protection
jurisdiction: Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies
applies_to: Owners and operators of personal data
key_requirements: Collection and processing with data-subject consent; rights of access, clarification, blocking and destruction; information requests answered within 3 working days (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies (designated body, status to verify)
penalties_range: Low administrative penalties; amounts not found (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Distinct category: genetic data defined as inherited or acquired genetic characteristics from analysis of a biological sample (art. 1); listed with special and biometric categories
notes: Regulator determined by presidential designation; enforcement reported as minimal; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. 998-IIIQ of 11 May 2010 on Personal Data
jurisdiction: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport (formerly Ministry of Transport, Communications and High Technologies)
applies_to: Owners and operators of personal data information systems
key_requirements: Consent for processing; registration of personal data information systems; security requirements (Cabinet Decree No. 161 of 6 Sep 2010; registration rules Decree No. 149 of 17 Aug 2010)
enforcement_authority: Ministry of Transport, Communications and High Technologies (regulator per DataGuidance 2023)
penalties_range: Not specified
notes: One unverified secondary source says National Cybersecurity Agency is regulator in 2026 and lists amendments through Law No. 1193-VIQD of 28 June 2024; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law on Personal Data Protection (2021)
jurisdiction: National Human Rights Commission of Mongolia
applies_to: Individuals, legal entities and organizations collecting or processing personal data in Mongolia, including representative offices and permanent establishments
key_requirements: Consent for processing; transfers abroad require data-subject consent unless law or treaty allows; security measures
enforcement_authority: National Human Rights Commission of Mongolia (NHRCM)
penalties_range: Fines of MNT 500,000 to MNT 20,000,000 (single compliance-site source) (unconfirmed)
notes: Replaced the 1995 Law on Personal Secrecy; sources differ on regulator

law_name: Law on Electronic Data Protection No. 25/NA (2017)
scope: Individuals and organisations whose electronic data is handled in Lao PDR
applies_to: Individuals, organisations and legal entities handling electronic data in Laos, including foreign entities engaged in covered activities
key_requirements: Principles for collection, processing and protection of electronic data; personal data may be accessed, used or disclosed on proper identification (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Ministry of Technology and Communications (MTC)
penalties_range: UNKNOWN; unverified claim of 10% turnover penalties from 2021 amendments (unconfirmed)
notes: Covers electronic data only; rest is thin secondary-source information; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. 149 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection (Ley 149 De Protección de Datos Personales)
scope: Natural persons (data subjects) regarding their personal data
applies_to: Public and private bodies and natural/legal persons that process personal data
key_requirements: 12 data protection principles; consent (express or tacit) with exceptions; data owner rights; security; cross-border transfers authorised by public bodies
retention_period: Default five years where no specific legal rule applies (article not found)
enforcement_authority: Ministry of Justice (MINJUS); no new dedicated authority created (older DLA Piper entry names the Ministry of Communications)
penalties_range: Fines reportedly up to CUP 20,000 (single secondary mention; unverified) (unconfirmed)
deceased_data: Law reportedly addresses personal data of deceased persons (article and duration not found) (unconfirmed)
notes: Approved by National Assembly 2022-05-14; published Gaceta Oficial Ordinaria No. 90 of 2022-08-25; entered into force 180 days later with its Regulation; Ministry of Communications Resolution 58/2022 covers electronic data security

law_name: Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 13 of 2011; Chap. 22:04)
jurisdiction: Office of the Information Commissioner (not yet established)
scope: Individuals (personal privacy and sensitive personal information)
key_requirements: General privacy principles; consent for sensitive personal information; Information Commissioner oversight (most operative provisions not yet proclaimed)
data_categories: Personal information (incl. DNA, fingerprints, blood type); sensitive personal information (health, racial/ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation, criminal/financial records)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Information Commissioner (vacant/not established; Ministry of Digital Transformation responsible)
penalties_range: Up to TTD 50,000 and 3 years imprisonment reported by one commercial site; penalty Part V not proclaimed (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Court/tribunal proceedings and judges' personal notes (s. 5); law enforcement collection exception (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Sensitive information may be processed without consent for research or statistical analysis (section not found); archival/historical disclosure provision in revised text s. 44 (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: DNA included in the definition of personal information; no specific genetic rule found (unconfirmed)
notes: Only partially proclaimed: Part I and ss. 7-18, 22, 23, 25(1), 26, 28 by LN 2/2012 (2012-01-06); s. 42(a),(b) by LN 220/2021; remainder not in force as of Feb 2025

law_name: Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023), Title III on personal data protection
jurisdiction: Data Protection Authority (APD) - functions temporarily held by ARPTIC
applies_to: Controllers and processors of personal data in the DRC (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Prior declaration or authorisation for processing (authorisation for sensitive/genetic data and third-country transfers); data subject rights incl. erasure; prohibition in principle of processing data on racial or ethnic origin and political opinions
data_categories: Personal data (art. 183: identification, contact, professional, billing and bank data, family circumstances, court decisions); biometric data; sensitive data
enforcement_authority: Data Protection Authority (APD); temporarily Autorite de regulation de la poste et des telecommunications / numerique (ARPTIC) by Ministerial Decree of 17 August 2024
penalties_range: Fines of CDF 8,000,000 to CDF 200,000,000
exemptions: Public security, defence, criminal investigations and sanctions enforcement (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Processing requires prior authorisation of the authority (DLA Piper)
notes: Law embedded in the Digital Code, not a standalone act; APD not formally created and implementing decrees largely missing; DRC ratified the Malabo Convention in 2023

law_name: Data Protection Act 2024
applies_to: Controllers and processors in Malawi and foreign entities offering goods or services to, or monitoring, individuals in Malawi
key_requirements: Lawful bases and consent; data subject rights (access/portability within 30 days, rectification within 14 days, erasure); 72-hour breach notification to authority and data subjects; cross-border transfer conditions; registration for controllers of significant importance
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive personal data (biometric, race or ethnic origin, religion, health status, political opinions)
enforcement_authority: Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA)
penalties_range: Reported fines up to MWK 5,000,000 and/or 12 months imprisonment (unverified vendor source) (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Processing solely for personal or household purposes; mere transmission of data through Malawi
notes: Assent date conflicting (31 Jan vs 1 Feb 2024); gazetted Feb 2024; commencement by Government Notice No. 40 of 2024; significant-importance entities must comply within 6 months, others within 24 months

law_name: Data Protection Act 2023 (Law No. 005 of 2023)
applies_to: Controllers and processors operating in Somalia; extra duties (DPO, impact assessments) for controllers of major importance
key_requirements: Breach notification within 72 hours; DPO and DPIA for major-importance controllers; cross-border transfers only to adequate countries or with safeguards or consent (arts. 30-31); registration of controllers and processors
enforcement_authority: Somalia Data Protection Authority (DPA)
penalties_range: Authority may investigate and impose fines; amounts not found (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Exemptions in art. 5(1)-(3) including personal or household use (unconfirmed)
notes: Signing date reported as 20, 21 or 23 March 2023; Authority launched Feb 2024; Implementation Regulation, Guidance and ADR Procedure issued; Council of Ministers approved a public-data regulatory framework in early 2026; controller registration began May 2026

law_name: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on Personal Data Protection
applies_to: All public and private controllers and processors (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Prior authorisation or declaration to the Authority (arts. 19, 27); transfers abroad only to adequate-protection countries (art. 32); consent rules with no legitimate-interest basis (vendor source) (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Autorite de protection des donnees a caractere personnel (APDP) - independent public body (art. 53)
penalties_range: Sources conflict: fines up to XAF 1 billion (Afriwise) or XAF 100 million and up to 10 years imprisonment (ConsentStack) (unconfirmed)
notes: 18-month transition ended 23 June 2026; authority creation reported but operational status unclear; Law 2010/012 (cybersecurity and cybercrime) still relevant; draft DPO requirement dropped

law_name: Law No. 007/PR/2015 on the Protection of Personal Data
jurisdiction: Agence nationale de securite informatique et de certification electronique (ANSICE)
applies_to: Controllers and processors operating in Chad (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Written declaration to ANSICE for most processing; prior authorisation for genetic/biometric data, health research, offence records, national ID numbers; data subject rights and security obligations
data_categories: Personal data; genetic and biometric data; health data; offence and conviction records
retention_period: Data kept only as long as necessary for the purpose (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Agence nationale de securite informatique et de certification electronique (ANSICE)
penalties_range: Administrative: warning, formal notice, processing ban, fines of XAF 1,000,000 to 10,000,000; criminal: imprisonment of 3 months to 1 year
exemptions: National defence or public safety processing excluded (one source; disputed) (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Health research requires prior ANSICE authorisation (no exemption found) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Processing requires prior authorisation of ANSICE
notes: Adopted by National Assembly 24 Nov 2014; implementing Decree No. 075/PR/2019 of 21 January 2019 (art. 5 corrected by Decree 1619/PR/2019); sources conflict on DPO and breach notification

law_name: Law No. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on the Protection of Personal Data (amended by Law No. 2023-31 of 4 July 2023 and Ordinances 2024-16 and 2024-29)
scope: Data subjects (natural persons) whose personal data are processed in Niger (unconfirmed)
applies_to: Public and private controllers and processors (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Data-subject rights: access, rectification/erasure, objection and opposition to direct marketing; controllers report annually to HAPDP on data kept beyond the period HAPDP sets (art. 64) (unconfirmed)
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (e.g. health, religion, political affiliation)
retention_period: Period fixed by HAPDP; controller reports annually on data kept beyond it (art. 64 per DLA Piper) (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: High Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (HAPDP), independent administrative authority attached to the Presidency; 11 members (art. 7 as amended)
penalties_range: Not specified
notes: Replaced Law No. 2017-28; Law 2023-31 amended arts 6, 7, 14, 23, 24 and 111; no official English translation; HAPDP site hapdp.ne reportedly hosts the text but was not verified; promulgation and entry-into-force dates not found; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 on the Protection of Persons with regard to the Processing of Personal Data
scope: Data subjects (natural persons) in Burkina Faso
applies_to: Controllers established in Burkina Faso and controllers abroad processing from national territory (art. 3)
key_requirements: Prior formalities with CIL before processing; regulated cross-border transfers (contract with foreign recipient with data-return clause, encryption); fuller right to information; health data hosted in Burkina Faso unless CIL exempts
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; health data
enforcement_authority: Commission for Informatics and Liberties (CIL)
penalties_range: Fixed fines of CFA 5 million to 100 million (per CIL president); other criminal sanctions not verified
notes: Repealed and replaced Law No. 010-2004/AN; adoption by the Assembly 30 March 2021, effective date 21 April 2021 given only by secondary sources (DataGuidance, ConsentStack); ConsentStack turnover-percentage fines unverified and not used; enforcement described as nascent

law_name: Law No. 2013-015 of 21 May 2013 on the Protection of Personal Data in the Republic of Mali (amended by Law No. 2017-070 of 18 December 2017)
applies_to: State, local authorities, public bodies, and private natural and legal persons processing data wholly or partly in Mali
key_requirements: Free right of access; rights to correct, update, block or delete inaccurate or unlawfully kept data; objection right including before first use for third-party prospecting; controller responds within 30 days; APDP approves transfers
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Authority (APDP)
penalties_range: APDP: warnings, formal notices, injunctions, withdrawal of approval; courts: fines of about CFA 2.5 million to 20 million plus imprisonment; obstructing APDP inspections CFA 5 million to 20 million (art. 65(7) as amended). 2025 fine of CFA 5 million on a clinic for undeclared CCTV
exemptions: Purely personal or domestic activity, unless data are systematically shared with third parties for dissemination (unconfirmed)
notes: DataGuidance dates the law 23 May 2013; APDP began operating only in 2016; no official English translation; ConsentStack page contains an ARTCI error and was not used; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. L/2016/037/AN on Cybersecurity and the Protection of Personal Data
applies_to: Controllers processing personal data (Part 2 of the law, 65 articles) (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Free right to object to processing for prospecting; direct prospecting without prior written consent is punished; restrictions on cross-border transfers (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: None operational: art. 47 provides for an authority to be set up by regulation but it is not yet established (DLA Piper, dataprotection.africa)
penalties_range: Direct prospecting without prior written consent: 1 to 5 years imprisonment and a fine (amount not found)
notes: Dates conflict (26 vs 28 July 2016); ConsentStack claims a CNIL Guinea but this contradicts DLA Piper; 2025 minister mentioned a new personal data bill, not verified as adopted; no official English translation

law_name: Law No. 1/03 of 10 March 2026 on the Protection of Personal Data
jurisdiction: Independent oversight authority (not yet confirmed operational)
applies_to: Public and private bodies and natural persons, for automated and non-automated processing, including controllers using processing means located in Burundi
key_requirements: Not specified
enforcement_authority: Independent administrative authority created by the law (press: Agency for the Protection of Personal Data; ARCT mentioned by trackers); no operational body confirmed
penalties_range: Criminal penalties for violations, amounts not found; Penal Code and ICT-offences law still apply (unconfirmed)
notes: National Assembly adopted the bill unanimously on 15 January 2026; no gazette text seen; language inferred from French-language press coverage

law_name: Law No. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018 on the Digital Code (Book V on personal data protection, arts 379-490), amended by Law No. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021
applies_to: Public and private bodies processing personal data by automated or non-automated means
key_requirements: APDP oversight of collection, processing, transmission, storage and use of personal data; regulation of sensitive data and international transfers with specified exceptions
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Authority (APDP), independent administrative authority
penalties_range: Repeat offences within 5 years: up to CFA 100 million or 5% of pre-tax sales, capped at CFA 100 million (secondary source, no article) (unconfirmed)
notes: Parliament adopted 13 June 2017; presidential assent 23 April 2018; Law 2020-35 amended arts 121, 125, 464 (APDP reduced from 11 to 8 members); also Law No. 2009-09 of 22 May 2009; Benin APDP is observer at Convention 108 Committee but accession not confirmed; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on the Protection of Personal Data
key_requirements: Consent, transparency and security (ch. II); prior declaration to IPDCP with receipt within one month; prior authorization for genetic, health, criminal or biometric data; rights to information (art. 35), access (art. 39), objection, erasure, rectification
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data incl. genetic, health, criminal, biometric
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Authority (IPDCP, Instance de protection des donnees a caractere personnel); launched activities 28 March 2025
penalties_range: Unlawful collection or retention of sensitive data without explicit consent: 1 to 5 years prison and fine of CFA 1 to 10 million, same for retention beyond legal periods and fraudulent CCTV (per IPDCP); a secondary tracker gives CFA 1 to 25 million (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Some processing exempt from declaration (articles not found) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic data requires prior authorization from IPDCP; genetic identity is part of the definition of personal data (art. 4)
notes: 8 chapters, 96 articles; published Journal officiel no. 26 ter of 29 Oct 2019; effective date not found; one tracker lists Togo as not party to Convention 108; mandatory CCTV declaration began July 2025; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Law No. 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 on the Protection of Personal Data
applies_to: Natural persons, the State, local authorities and public or private legal persons, including controllers established or using processing means in Mauritania
key_requirements: Access requests (arts 53-58), objection (art. 59), rectification and deletion (arts 61-63) with a one-month controller response; breach notification duties reported
enforcement_authority: Personal Data Protection Authority (APD), created by art. 64; constituted in February 2022 (decree 2022-013)
penalties_range: Not specified
notes: Published in Journal officiel no. 1400 of 15 November 2017; APD internal rules dated 23 Oct 2023; Malabo ratification claims conflict (9 May 2023 vs 15th ratifier), not used; old DataGuidance entry calling the law a bill is outdated; effective_date not found: the enactment date is used

law_name: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025
jurisdiction: Information Commission (designated National Data Protection Commission)
scope: Data subjects in The Gambia (extraterritorial: foreign controllers processing data of people in The Gambia)
applies_to: All public and private controllers and processors; excludes purely personal/household activity and anonymous data
key_requirements: Lawful processing and accountability without prior registration; breach notification to the Commission within 72 hours; impact assessments for high-risk processing (unconfirmed)
data_categories: Personal data; special categories of personal data (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Information Commission
penalties_range: Reported administrative fines up to 4% of global turnover for serious violations; criminal penalties up to 10 years for selling personal data (sources conflict, unverified) (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Purely personal or household activity; anonymous data
notes: Passed unanimously by National Assembly 29 September 2025; assent reported 7 November 2025 by secondary sources only; no commencement order or gazette found.

law_name: Law No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the Protection of Personal Data as amended by Law No. 025/2023 of 12 July 2023
jurisdiction: Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy (APDPVP)
scope: Data subjects whose personal data is processed in Gabon
applies_to: All public and private entities processing personal data
key_requirements: Declaration/authorisation to the authority; data subject rights of access, correction, erasure and objection (one month to respond); special measures for children's data
enforcement_authority: Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy (APDPVP)
penalties_range: Reported fines of CFA 1 million to 100 million (rising for repeat violations), suspension of processing and criminal penalties; secondary sources (unconfirmed)
notes: Amends Law 001/2011; some sources date the 2023 law 9 July 2023; published in Journal Officiel 15 July 2023; Ordinance 00002/PR/2020 also amended the 2011 law; former regulator CNPDCP replaced by APDPVP.

law_name: Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012)
jurisdiction: Data Protection Commission (provided by the Act but never established)
scope: Data subjects (individuals) whose personal information is processed (unconfirmed)
key_requirements: Consent, purpose limitation, minimisation and integrity; data subject rights of access, correction and objection to direct marketing; prohibition on processing sensitive information unless permitted (s. 29)
enforcement_authority: Data Protection Commission (not yet appointed)
penalties_range: Commission cannot impose fines; enforcement through the courts (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Personal/household activity, de-identified data, national security and public safety, journalistic/artistic/literary purposes (s. 4)
research_exemption: No research exemption among the general exemptions in s. 4 (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Covered as sensitive personal information; processing prohibited unless permitted by the Act (s. 29) (unconfirmed)
notes: Cited as the 2011 Act but published as Act 5 of 2012; one aggregator wrongly gives Act No. 31 of 2011; ConsentStack gives 1 January 2012; Commission never established so law largely unenforced.

law_name: Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (VCDPA), Va. Code 59.1-575 et seq. (2021 Acts ch. 35 and 36; HB 2307/SB 1392)
scope: Residents of Virginia acting in an individual or household context (not commercial or employment context)
applies_to: Controllers/processors doing business in Virginia or targeting Virginia residents that control or process data of at least 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 consumers plus over 50% of gross revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Consent for sensitive data (59.1-578); rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out of targeted ads/sale/profiling (59.1-577); data protection assessments and reasonable security (59.1-578). No breach-notification duty in the Act
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous data; de-identified data; children's data (under 13, COPPA-aligned)
retention_period: No fixed period; collection limited to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose (59.1-578(A)(1))
enforcement_authority: Office of the Attorney General of Virginia
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after 30-day cure period; injunctive relief; no private right of action (59.1-584)
exemptions: Government bodies, financial institutions under GLBA, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, higher-education institutions, employment and B2B data (59.1-576)
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts processing for scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest by peer-reviewed or IRB-type study (59.1-582)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify a natural person is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent (59.1-575, 59.1-578)
notes: 2025 amendments (SB 854) restrict social media use by under-16s from 2026-01-01; check Oct 2026 status of litigation. HB 714 (2022) redirected penalties to a trust fund

law_name: Colorado Privacy Act (CPA), SB 21-190, C.R.S. 6-1-1301 et seq.
jurisdiction: Colorado Attorney General and district attorneys
scope: Residents of Colorado (consumers acting in individual or household context)
applies_to: Controllers conducting business in Colorado or targeting Colorado residents that process data of 100,000+ consumers per year, or any amount if they derive revenue or discounts from sale of personal data and process 25,000+ consumers
key_requirements: Opt-in consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out of targeted ads/sale/profiling, incl. universal opt-out mechanism (from 2024-07-01); data protection assessments and security (6-1-1308)
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous data; de-identified data; biological and neural data (HB 24-1058); minors' data (SB 24-041)
retention_period: Data minimization: collection adequate, relevant and limited to what is reasonably necessary; no longer than necessary for the specified purpose (6-1-1308(3))
enforcement_authority: Colorado Department of Law, Office of the Attorney General (AG rulemaking under 4 CCR 904-3) and district attorneys
penalties_range: Violation is a deceptive trade practice under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act: civil penalty up to $20,000 per violation (6-1-112); no private right of action; mandatory cure period ended 2025-01-01
exemptions: GLBA/HIPAA-regulated data and entities, employment and B2B data, state and local governments, nonprofits not exempt, higher-education/public-interest research (6-1-1304)
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts public or peer-reviewed scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest, with consent/ethics safeguards (6-1-1304)
genetic_data: Genetic data is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent; biological data (incl. genetic) added by HB 24-1058 (6-1-1303)
notes: Search sources conflicted ($2,000 vs $20,000 per violation, and signing date July 7 vs July 8); $20,000 under CCPA 6-1-112 is the figure used. Later amendments for minors and neural data

law_name: Connecticut Data Privacy Act (CTDPA), Public Act 22-15 (SB 6), Conn. Gen. Stat. 42-515 et seq.; amended by Public Act 25-113 (SB 1295)
scope: Residents of Connecticut acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Since 2026-07-01: persons doing business in Connecticut or targeting residents that process data of 35,000+ consumers, or any amount if they process sensitive data or sell personal data
key_requirements: Consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out, plus list of third parties receiving data and profiling rights (2026); data protection and profiling impact assessments; reasonable security
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous data; de-identified data; consumer health data; minors' data (under 18)
retention_period: Data minimization: limit collection to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose (42-520)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Attorney General of Connecticut (Privacy Section)
penalties_range: Violation is an unfair trade practice under CUTPA: up to $5,000 per willful violation (42-110o); no private right of action
exemptions: Government bodies, nonprofits (before 2026 amendments), GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, employment and B2B data (42-517)
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts public or peer-reviewed scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest, and certain research data (42-517)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify an individual is sensitive data requiring consent (42-515)
notes: PA 25-113 signed June 2025 (sources say June 24 or 25), main changes effective 2026-07-01; SB 4 (signed 2026-05-27 per one source) adds further CTDPA changes from 2026-10-01. website_url is the AG page not seen in results

law_name: Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UCPA), SB 227 (2022), Utah Code 13-61-101 et seq.
jurisdiction: Utah Attorney General; Division of Consumer Protection (complaint intake)
scope: Residents of Utah acting in an individual or household context
applies_to: Controllers/processors with annual revenue of $25M+ that do business in Utah and process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers with over 50% revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Notice and opt-out model: rights to access, delete, port, opt out of targeted ads/sale and sensitive-data processing; privacy notice; reasonable security. No assessments or opt-in consent
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; aggregated and de-identified data
retention_period: No retention rule; no explicit data minimization duty beyond purpose disclosure (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Utah Office of the Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to $7,500 per violation after 30-day cure period; no private right of action
exemptions: Government, nonprofits, higher education, GLBA/HIPAA entities and data, employment and B2B data, small businesses under $25M revenue
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest following ethics/IRB-type oversight (13-61-304) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic personal data and biometric data are sensitive data; controller must give notice and opt-out (not opt-in consent)
notes: 2024 amendments (SB 149/SB 194) and 2025 amendments adjusted scope; July 2025 AG/Division report recommended further changes

law_name: Iowa Consumer Data Protection Act, Senate File 262 (2023), Iowa Code chapter 715D
scope: Residents of Iowa acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Persons doing business in Iowa or targeting residents that control/process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers with over 50% revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Notice and opt-out model: rights to access, delete, port, opt out of sale and sensitive-data processing; privacy notice; reasonable security. No assessments duty for most controllers (715D.4)
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; de-identified and pseudonymous data
retention_period: Data minimization: collection limited to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (715D.4)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Attorney General of Iowa
penalties_range: Up to $7,500 per violation after 90-day cure period; no private right of action (715D.8)
exemptions: Government, financial institutions/GLBA, HIPAA entities, nonprofits, higher education, employment and B2B data (715D.2)
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest under ethics/IRB-type oversight (715D.7) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify a person is sensitive data; opt-out of processing after notice (not opt-in)
notes: Signing date March 28 or 29, 2023 differs between sources; penalty figure verified only in secondary sources

law_name: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act (INCDPA), Senate Enrolled Act 5 (2023), IC 24-15
scope: Residents of Indiana acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Persons doing business in Indiana or targeting residents that control/process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers with over 50% revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Opt-in consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out of targeted ads/sale/profiling; data protection assessments; reasonable security
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous and de-identified data
retention_period: Data minimization: collection limited to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (IC 24-15-4) (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Indiana Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to $7,500 per violation after 30-day cure period; AG exclusive enforcement, no private right of action
exemptions: Government, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, nonprofits, higher education, employment and B2B data
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest with ethics/IRB-type oversight (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify a person is sensitive data requiring consent
notes: Sources are secondary trackers; $7,500 and cure period not checked in IC 24-15 text

law_name: Tennessee Information Protection Act (TIPA), HB 1181/SB 73 (2023), Tenn. Code Ann. 47-18-3201 et seq.
scope: Residents of Tennessee acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Persons doing business in Tennessee or targeting residents with revenue over $25M that control/process data of 175,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers with over 50% revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Opt-in consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out; data protection assessments; privacy program aligned to NIST Privacy Framework gives affirmative defense
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous and de-identified data
retention_period: Data minimization: limit collection to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Tennessee Attorney General and Reporter
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after 60-day cure period; treble damages for willful or knowing violations; no private right of action
exemptions: Government, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, nonprofits, higher education, employment and B2B data, small businesses under thresholds
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest following ethics/IRB-type oversight (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify a person is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent
notes: One 2024 guide lists $15,000 per violation; $7,500 (plus treble damages) is better supported

law_name: Montana Consumer Data Privacy Act (MCDPA), SB 384 (2023), Mont. Code Ann. Title 30, ch. 14, part 28; amended by SB 297 (2025)
jurisdiction: Montana Attorney General (Department of Justice, Office of Consumer Protection)
scope: Residents of Montana acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Persons doing business in Montana or targeting residents that control/process data of 50,000+ consumers (25,000+ from 2025-10-01), or 15,000+ with over 25% revenue from sale of personal data (post-SB 297)
key_requirements: Opt-in consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out of targeted ads/sale/profiling; data protection assessments; minors' protections added by SB 297
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; minors' data; pseudonymous and de-identified data
retention_period: Data minimization: limit collection to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary; no fixed period (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Montana Department of Justice, Office of Consumer Protection (Attorney General)
penalties_range: AG may seek injunction, civil penalties (summary cites up to $7,500 per violation) and fees; SB 297 removed the cure period; no private right of action (unconfirmed)
exemptions: Government, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, nonprofits (partially), higher education, employment and B2B data
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest under ethics/IRB-type oversight (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent
notes: SB 297 effective 2025-10-01; its signing date was reported as May 8 (2025) by one source only

law_name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act (TDPSA), HB 4 (2023), Tex. Bus. & Com. Code ch. 541
scope: Residents of Texas acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Persons doing business in Texas or offering products/services to Texas residents that process or sell personal data and are not small businesses as defined by the U.S. SBA (no consumer-count threshold)
key_requirements: Opt-in consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out; universal opt-out signals from 2025-01-01; data protection assessments; reasonable security
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; pseudonymous and de-identified data
retention_period: Data minimization: limit collection to what is adequate, reasonably necessary and proportionate to disclosed purposes (541.101) (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Texas Attorney General
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after 30-day cure period; injunctive relief; no private right of action
exemptions: State agencies and political subdivisions, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, nonprofits, higher education, electric utilities, employment and B2B data, SBA small businesses (except sale of sensitive data needs consent)
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest under ethics/IRB-type oversight (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify an individual is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent
notes: One source gave June 13 as signing date; most give June 18, 2023. Chapter 541 citation from prior knowledge, not confirmed in results

law_name: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (OCPA), SB 619 (2023), ORS 646A.570 to 646A.589
scope: Residents of Oregon acting in individual or household context
applies_to: Persons doing business in Oregon or serving Oregon residents that control/process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers with 25% or more revenue from sale of personal data; nonprofits covered from 2025-07-01
key_requirements: Opt-in consent for sensitive data; rights to access, correct, delete, port, opt out, and to receive a list of specific third parties receiving data; data protection assessments; global opt-out signals from 2026-01-01
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data; derived data; de-identified data
retention_period: Data minimization: collection limited to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (ORS 646A.578) (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Oregon Department of Justice, Attorney General
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation, plus injunction, restitution or disgorgement; cure period lapsed 2026-01-01; no private right of action
exemptions: Government bodies, GLBA financial institutions (not mere GLBA data), HIPAA data, employment data, certain nonprofits and insurers, ORS 646A.572
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living consumers (residents acting in an individual or household context) only; employee and B2B data excluded
research_exemption: Exempts research in the public interest meeting ethics/IRB-type conditions (ORS 646A.572) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic and biometric data are sensitive data requiring opt-in consent
notes: One vendor source gave March 8, 2023 as signing date; others say July 18, 2023. 2025 amendments (HB 2008) reportedly ban sale of precise geolocation and under-16 data from 2026, not confirmed in results

law_name: Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act (HB 154, 6 Del. C. ch. 12D)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in Delaware or targeting Delaware residents that control/process data of 35,000+ consumers, or 10,000+ consumers with over 20% of revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale and profiling; consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments; 60-day cure period lapsed 2025-12-31 (discretionary since 2026-01-01)
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic data and biometric data, known child data, precise geolocation)
enforcement_authority: Delaware Department of Justice, Consumer Protection Unit
penalties_range: No fixed penalty in the Act; violation is an unlawful practice under Delaware consumer protection law (reported up to USD 10,000 per willful violation); no private right of action
exemptions: Government bodies, HIPAA entities and PHI, GLBA financial institutions, clinical research under Common Rule/ICH, deidentified and publicly available data
research_exemption: Clinical research already subject to Common Rule or ICH standards is exempt (secondary source)
genetic_data: Genetic data is defined separately and is sensitive data requiring consent
notes: HB 380 (2026) to lower thresholds passed the House 2026-05-21; pending in Senate per secondary source

law_name: New Jersey Data Privacy Act (P.L. 2023, c.266, S332; N.J.S.A. 56:8-166.4 et seq.)
jurisdiction: New Jersey Attorney General (Division of Consumer Affairs)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Controllers doing business in NJ or targeting NJ residents that process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers and derive revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments; 30-day cure period sunset 2026-07-15
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data processed for identification)
enforcement_authority: New Jersey Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to USD 10,000 per first violation and USD 20,000 per subsequent violation under the NJ Consumer Fraud Act; no private right of action
exemptions: GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA, certain data types; internal research to develop or improve products is a permitted use
research_exemption: Only a general internal-research use carve-out found; no genetic-specific research exemption found
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data processed to identify a person is sensitive data requiring consent
notes: Assembly Bill 5017 (2024-25 session) would amend the Act; status not confirmed

law_name: New Hampshire Privacy Act (SB 255, RSA 507-H)
jurisdiction: New Hampshire Department of Justice (Attorney General)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Controllers doing business in NH or targeting NH residents above consumer-count thresholds (sources conflict: 35,000 consumers, or 10,000 with over 25% of revenue from sale of data)
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments; mandatory cure period ended 2026-01-01, now AG discretion
enforcement_authority: New Hampshire Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to USD 10,000 per violation as unfair or deceptive practice under RSA 358-A; no private right of action
exemptions: GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, nonprofits, higher education, FERPA/FCRA/DPPA/Farm Credit Act data
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data is sensitive data (consent required) when processed to uniquely identify an individual
notes: Thresholds conflict between sources; verify against RSA 507-H

law_name: Kentucky Consumer Data Privacy Act (HB 15, 2024 Regular Session)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in KY or targeting KY residents that control/process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers and over 50% of revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments; 30-day cure period (does not sunset)
enforcement_authority: Kentucky Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to USD 7,500 per violation; penalties go to a consumer privacy fund; no private right of action
exemptions: State agencies and political subdivisions, HIPAA entities, GLBA financial institutions, nonprofits, higher education
research_exemption: Research data reportedly exempt (low-reliability summary; check KRS 367.3611 et seq.)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data is sensitive data (consent required) when processed to uniquely identify a specific person
notes: Some sources call it the Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act

law_name: Nebraska Data Privacy Act (LB 1074)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in NE that process personal data and are not small businesses under the federal Small Business Act; small businesses may not sell sensitive data without consent
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments; 30-day cure period (does not sunset)
enforcement_authority: Nebraska Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to USD 7,500 per violation not cured within 30 days; injunctive relief and fees; no private right of action
exemptions: GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA, small businesses (except sensitive data sale), federal research-law data
research_exemption: Data collected under federal research laws such as the Common Rule is exempt (secondary source)
genetic_data: Sensitive data only when processed to uniquely identify an individual; consent required

law_name: Maryland Online Data Privacy Act of 2024 (MODPA, HB 567)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in MD or targeting MD residents that handle data of 35,000+ consumers, or 10,000+ consumers with over 20% of revenue from sale of personal data
key_requirements: Data minimization (collection limited to what is reasonably necessary; sensitive data only when strictly necessary); ban on sale of sensitive data; consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic and biometric data); minors data
enforcement_authority: Maryland Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
penalties_range: Up to USD 10,000 per violation and USD 25,000 per repeated violation under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; misdemeanor fine up to USD 1,000 or 1 year prison reported; no private right of action
exemptions: GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, registered national securities associations
genetic_data: Any genetic or biometric data is sensitive data, regardless of identification purpose; processing only if strictly necessary and sale is banned even with consent
notes: Law took effect 2025-10-01 but applies to processing from 2026-04-01; cure period (60 days, if AG finds cure possible) sunsets 2027-04-01

law_name: Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act (HF 4757, Minn. Stat. ch. 325M, secs. 325M.10-325M.21)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Entities doing business in MN or targeting MN residents that process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers and over 25% of revenue from sale of personal data; small businesses exempt
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; opt-in consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments
enforcement_authority: Minnesota Attorney General
penalties_range: Civil penalties up to USD 7,500 per violation; no private right of action
exemptions: Banks and credit unions, GLBA data, small businesses (SBA), payment-only transactions (sec. 325M.12)
research_exemption: Internal research to develop or improve products is a permitted purpose (sec. 325M.19); federal human-subjects research entities exempt in the separate genetic law, sec. 325F.995
genetic_data: Sensitive data when processed to uniquely identify an individual (consent required); separate Genetic Information Privacy Act at Minn. Stat. 325F.995
notes: Clifford Chance dates enactment 2024-05-19 (legislature adoption); Walz signature 2024-05-24. HF 2700 (2025) would add consumer health data; in committee

law_name: Rhode Island Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act (H 7787, R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 6-48.1)
scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in RI or targeting RI residents that process data of 35,000+ consumers, or 10,000+ consumers and over 20% of revenue from sale of personal data; commercial websites and ISPs have disclosure duties
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; privacy notice naming third parties; most sources report no cure period
enforcement_authority: Rhode Island Attorney General
penalties_range: Up to USD 10,000 per violation as deceptive trade practice (sources conflict; one lists USD 100-500); no private right of action
exemptions: GLBA, HIPAA and other data-level exemptions including research data
research_exemption: Data-level exemption for research data (scope not confirmed)
genetic_data: Sensitive data requiring opt-in consent only when processed for identification
notes: Enactment date disputed: one source says bill became law without governor signature (transmitted 2024-06-25); cure period sources conflict

law_name: Biometric Information Privacy Act (740 ILCS 14; Public Act 95-994)
jurisdiction: Private right of action in Illinois state circuit court or federal court (740 ILCS 14/20); no regulator
scope: Individuals whose biometric identifiers or information are collected by private entities in Illinois
applies_to: Private entities (not state/local government or Illinois courts)
key_requirements: Written informed consent before collecting biometric data; published retention schedule and destruction guidelines (destroy at end of purpose or within 3 years of last interaction); no sale or profit from biometric data
data_categories: Biometric identifiers (retina/iris scan, fingerprint, voiceprint, hand or face geometry scan) and biometric information
retention_period: Destroy when initial purpose is satisfied or within 3 years of last interaction, whichever is first (sec. 15(a))
enforcement_authority: Aggrieved individuals via courts (private right of action, sec. 20)
penalties_range: Liquidated damages USD 1,000 per negligent violation or USD 5,000 per intentional/reckless violation, or actual damages, plus fees; since Public Act 103-0769 (2024-08-02) counted once per person, not per scan
exemptions: Government agencies and Illinois courts; photographs, signatures, human biological samples used for valid scientific testing or screening, demographic data, physical descriptions
research_exemption: Human biological samples used for valid scientific testing or screening are excluded from biometric identifiers (sec. 10)
genetic_data: Not biometric identifiers when from biological samples for scientific testing; genetic testing is governed by the separate GIPA (410 ILCS 513)
notes: Effective date assumed equal to approval date; no express effective-date text seen. Amended by P.A. 103-0769 (2024-08-02)

law_name: My Health My Data Act (HB 1155, RCW ch. 19.373)
jurisdiction: Washington Attorney General; also private right of action via Consumer Protection Act (RCW 19.86)
scope: Washington consumers and persons whose consumer health data is collected in Washington
applies_to: Regulated entities doing business in WA or targeting WA consumers; small businesses from 2024-06-30
key_requirements: Consumer health data privacy policy; consent for collection and sharing; separate valid authorization for sale; rights of access and deletion; geofencing ban near health facilities
data_categories: Consumer health data (incl. biometric and genetic data)
enforcement_authority: Washington Attorney General and private plaintiffs under the Consumer Protection Act
penalties_range: AG civil penalty up to USD 7,500 per violation (RCW 19.86.140); private treble damages up to USD 25,000 plus fees; violation is per se CPA violation
exemptions: HIPAA PHI, chapter 70.02 RCW records, Common Rule data, 42 CFR Part 2, deidentified data (RCW 19.373.100)
research_exemption: Personal information used for public or peer-reviewed scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest is not consumer health data; research exemptions in RCW 19.373.100
genetic_data: Genetic and biometric data are expressly consumer health data (full definition text not seen)
notes: Private right of action; first lawsuit filed Feb 2025 per Orrick

law_name: Oklahoma Consumer Data Privacy Act (Senate Bill 546, 2026 Okla. Sess. Laws ch. 8; 75A O.S. ss. 300-320)
scope: Oklahoma residents acting in an individual or household context (not commercial or employment context)
applies_to: Businesses operating in Oklahoma or targeting Oklahoma residents that process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers per year, or at least 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from selling personal data (75A O.S. s. 314(A))
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale and certain profiling (45-day response plus 45-day extension; appeal process); opt-in consent for sensitive data; privacy notices, data minimization and data protection assessments
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data used to identify a person, precise geolocation); pseudonymous data
retention_period: No fixed period; collection limited to what is reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (data minimization); no specific retention schedule found (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Oklahoma Attorney General (exclusive enforcement; no private right of action)
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after a 30-day cure period (non-sunsetting); injunction, attorney fees and investigation costs
exemptions: State agencies and political subdivisions, nonprofits, institutions of higher education, HIPAA covered entities and data, GLBA financial institutions/data; employment and commercial contexts
deceased_data: Not covered in sources found: consumer defined as an Oklahoma natural person acting in an individual or household context; no deceased-person provision found (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Identifiable private information used in human subjects research is exempt; public-interest research permitted as a common business activity (section number not found)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data used to identify a person is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent before processing
notes: Not signed with an official short title per one source; Virginia-style with Texas elements; does not require honoring universal opt-out signals (GPC). Enrolled text on oklegislature.gov was not seen; dates and details come from law-firm summaries. Sources disagree on whether Oklahoma is the 20th or 21st state.

law_name: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act (House Bill 351, Act 2026-552)
scope: Alabama residents (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in Alabama or targeting Alabama residents that process personal data of more than 25,000 consumers (excluding payment-only data) or derive more than 25% of gross revenue from selling personal data; businesses under 500 employees and nonprofits under 100 employees exempt unless they sell data
key_requirements: Consumer rights to confirm, correct, delete and opt out; sensitive data consent; secure channels to exercise rights; Virginia-style model but no mandatory data protection assessments
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data used to identify an individual)
enforcement_authority: Alabama Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action)
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $15,000 per violation; 45-day cure period that does not sunset
exemptions: GLBA and HIPAA entities/data, small businesses under 500 employees and nonprofits under 100 employees (if not selling data), human subjects research data, patient safety work product (non-exhaustive list)
research_exemption: Identifiable data used for human subjects research is exempt (section number not found)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data used to identify an individual is sensitive data (consent required)
notes: Signing date reported as 2026-04-16 by most sources (FPF, Privacy Daily) and 2026-04-17 by Mayer Brown. Act number 2026-552 comes from a single source (privacylawmap). One local outlet claims effect on 2026-05-01 but others say 2027-05-01 (the latter used). Enrolled text on legislature site not seen.

law_name: Louisiana Data Privacy Act (Senate Bill 386, Act No. 502 of 2026; La. R.S. 51:1780.1-1780.5)
scope: Louisiana residents acting in an individual or household capacity (not commercial or employment context)
applies_to: Persons doing business in Louisiana meeting one of: annual gross revenue over $25 million; buying/selling/sharing personal information of 75,000+ consumers, households or devices; or 50%+ of revenue from selling personal information
key_requirements: Texas-style model: consumer rights (access, correct, delete, port, opt out); consent for sensitive data; data minimization, security and risk assessments
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data)
enforcement_authority: Louisiana Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action)
penalties_range: No penalty schedule in the Act itself; violations are unfair trade practices under LUTPA, civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation (R.S. 51:1407) reported, higher where elderly or disabled persons affected; cure period only 2027-01-01 to 2027-07-31 (30-day notice) (unconfirmed)
exemptions: State agencies and political subdivisions, GLBA financial institutions and data, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, higher education institutions, public utilities; certain research data
research_exemption: Certain research data exempt (exact scope and section not found) (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data included in sensitive data requiring consent
notes: Passed Senate 36-0 and House 94-0; signed 2026-05-29. Enrolled text on legis.la.gov was not seen. Sources disagree on penalty amounts (one cites $10,000 where elderly/disabled are affected) and one lists a private right of action while most exclude it; ranked 22nd state by most sources.

law_name: Vermont Data Privacy and Online Surveillance Act (S.71, Act 145 of 2026; 9 V.S.A. ch. 61A, ss. 2415a-2415k)
scope: Vermont residents (consumers); consumer health data provisions apply regardless of volume thresholds
applies_to: Entities doing business in Vermont or targeting Vermont residents that process personal data of 35,000+ consumers or sensitive data of 3,000+ consumers or sell data of 3,000+ consumers; consumer health data rules apply without thresholds
key_requirements: Connecticut-style model: consumer rights; consent for sensitive data (incl. genetic, biometric, neural, precise geolocation, consumer health, known child data) and limits to what is reasonably necessary; privacy notices must disclose LLM training use; bans manipulative design; no sale or targeted ads for ages 13-17
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (genetic, biometric, neural, precise geolocation, consumer health data, known child data)
enforcement_authority: Vermont Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action) under the Vermont Consumer Protection Act
penalties_range: Up to $10,000 per violation under the Consumer Protection Act; discretionary 60-day cure period 2028-01-01 to 2029-06-30
exemptions: Data-level exemptions: various health data, GLBA data, FCRA data, emergency contact information, post-secondary school enrollment/degree verification and related research services
research_exemption: No general research exemption found; only post-secondary school research services data exempt (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic and biometric data are sensitive data requiring consent before collection and sale; separate H.639 covers direct-to-consumer genetic testing
notes: Legislative record shows signed by Governor 2026-06-16. Sources disagree on state rank (21st/23rd/24th). Separate bill H.639 regulates direct-to-consumer genetic testing (effective 2026-07-01). Enacted text not read; details from law-firm summaries.

law_name: Florida Digital Bill of Rights (CS/CS/SB 262 'Technology Transparency', Ch. 2023-201, Laws of Fla.; Fla. Stat. ss. 501.701 et seq.)
jurisdiction: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Office of the Attorney General)
scope: Florida residents (consumers); narrow controller definition so applies to few businesses
applies_to: Controllers with over $1 billion global gross annual revenue that also derive 50%+ of revenue from online ad sales, operate a consumer smart speaker with voice assistant, or operate an app store with 250,000+ apps; some duties (e.g. sale of sensitive data) reach other for-profit businesses (s. 501.715)
key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out of sale, targeted ads and profiling; opt-in consent for sensitive data and its sale; data minimization, security and retention schedule; children's online protections
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic data processed to uniquely identify, health diagnoses, precise geolocation)
retention_period: Controllers and processors must adopt and follow a retention schedule; retention ends at the first of several triggers, including two years after the consumer's last interaction
enforcement_authority: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General); no private right of action
penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $50,000 per violation, tripled (up to $150,000) for violations involving a child, failure to delete/correct after verified request, or continued sale/sharing after opt-out; discretionary 45-day cure period (not granted for child-related violations)
exemptions: Entities below the $1 billion/prong thresholds; HIPAA and GLBA entities/data; research and other listed processing purposes (sections not confirmed) (unconfirmed)
research_exemption: Exemption for research purposes reported by one secondary source, section not confirmed (unconfirmed)
genetic_data: Genetic data is sensitive data only when processed to uniquely identify an individual; sale of sensitive data requires consent
notes: Limited-scope law; counted as a comprehensive privacy law by some sources and not by others. Enforcement rule Fla. Admin. Code 2-3.003 effective 2024-07-18. AG sued Roku under the Act in 2025 (reported settled 2026-06). No 2026 amendments found.
